hints: Focus on each C=C bond separately and ask where the Br can go when one HBr adds across it.
Check the two cyclohexene rings for symmetry. Adding Br to the two ends of the ring double bond gives two different positional isomers relative to the side chain.
Now combine the three additions and use the left-right symmetry of the whole molecule to see which left plus right plus middle combinations are truly identical.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three addition sites**

Molecule X has two identical cyclohexene double bonds at the ends and one central chain double bond in $-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-$. One mole of $HBr$ adds to each $C=C$, so the final product is a tribromide with unchanged carbon skeleton.

$$X + 3HBr \rightarrow XBr_3$$

**Count regioisomers for each double bond**

For a cyclohex-3-en-1-yl ring, the double bond is unsymmetrical with respect to the attachment at C1. Putting $Br$ on one end gives a 3-bromo-1-substituted ring, putting $Br$ on the other end gives a 4-bromo-1-substituted ring. So each ring has 2 structural options.

For the central bond, the two sides are both $-CH_2-(ring)$, so $Br$ on the left C and $Br$ on the right C look the same if the two ends are the same. On its own it gives 1 structural type.

**Combine with whole-molecule symmetry**

Call the ring options A (3-bromo) and B (4-bromo). The pair (Left, Right) can be flipped end to end, so (A,B) is the same as (B,A). This gives 3 ring-pair types: (A,A), (B,B), (A,B).

$$\text{ring pairs} = AA, BB, AB$$

**See why the middle Br creates an extra product**

If the two ends are the same, AA or BB, putting the central $Br$ nearer the left or nearer the right gives the same structure by flipping. That is 1 product each.

If the ends are different, AB, putting the central $Br$ nearer the A-ring is structurally different from putting it nearer the B-ring. That is 2 products.

$$Total = 1 (AA) + 1 (BB) + 2 (AB) = 4$$

options.A: 3 counts only the ring pairs AA, BB and AB but misses that the AB pair splits into two when the central Br is considered. When the ends are different, Br in the middle nearer the left is different from Br nearer the right.
options.B: Correct. Each end ring gives 2 positional isomers, giving AA, BB and AB pairs. AA gives 1, BB gives 1, and AB gives 2 depending on which side the central Br is closer to, for a total of 4 structural isomers.
options.C: 6 comes from overcounting, for example 2 x 3 or 3 x 2, and ignoring the left-right symmetry of X. (A,B) is identical to (B,A) by turning the molecule round, and the central bond does not give 2 independent isomers when the ends are identical.
options.D: 8 is 2 x 2 x 2, assuming each of the three C=C bonds independently gives 2 isomers with no symmetry. This ignores that the two ends of X are identical and the two ends of the central C=C are identical, so many of the 8 combinations are duplicates.
